accuracy.evidence: Checked against NASA Science 'Our Solar System' (the Sun, 8 planets, their moons, dwarf planets, asteroids and comets), the IAU 2006 planet definition, NASA/FAI use of the Kármán line at about 100 km as the start of space, typical cruising altitudes of 10 to 12 km, cloud tops mostly below 12 km and weather balloons reaching 30 to 40 km, and the DfE Year 5 Earth and space statements. The Moon is in the solar system (it orbits Earth, which orbits the Sun) and night-sky stars other than the Sun are outside it. The rocket and moving planets are marked not to scale in the adult text and on the find step.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early-years space ideas (Vosniadou and Brewer; Sharp 1996): Earth is not a planet because we live on it (step 3 prediction, p1, challenge notplanet), the Moon and stars sit in the sky with the clouds (step 2 prediction and Moon message, p4, m2, challenge moonsky and clouds), the night-sky stars belong to our solar system (step 4 prediction and star cards, m3, challenge allstars and roundearth), Earth is in the middle (m1, challenge earthmid) and the Moon is left out of the solar system (Moon build message, m6, challenge onearth).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagssys is about where space is and what the solar system includes: a rocket flown up past a bird, clouds, a plane and a balloon until the air runs out, an air-or-space sort, a five-level zoom from a house to the Sun and its planets, a membership build with two far stars kept outside, and tapping Earth among moving planets before naming the group. flagpname orders and names the planets, flagstar is about the Sun as a star, flagspin about Earth's spin and orbit; none has the rocket, zoom or membership build. Gate similarity is under 30% to every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner sees the sky darken and the 'space starts here' line only after passing the clouds and plane, has the Moon refused from the air box, watches home shrink to Earth, then to one of eight planets round the Sun, and finds that night-sky stars are refused from the solar system circle while the Moon is accepted. The closing line of each task names the idea just seen.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with tempting wrong options the lab then tests: 'clouds are in space because they are very high' (the rocket passes them well below the space line), 'the Moon is in the air with the clouds' (the sort places it in space), 'Earth is not a planet, it is where we live' (the zoom shows Earth as one of 8 planets) and 'night-sky stars are part of our solar system' (the build sends them far away).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with eleven distinct wrong-answer messages: Earth not a planet, Earth a star, all the stars, just Earth, space in the clouds, space past the stars, the Moon with the clouds, the Moon on Earth, stars going round Earth, Earth in the middle and the Moon in the middle. Each names the slip in kid words and restates the fact.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation reads at FK grade 0.9 and adult at 7.2 (family limits 5.0 and 10.0). Kid sentences are short and concrete (we live on Earth; the air runs out; the sky looks black). Canvas labels are two to four words, such as 'In the air', 'Out in space', 'Far away', 'Tap Earth, the blue planet'. The adult text names the key words and the scale caveat.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Each kid paragraph adds one idea: Earth is a planet, the solar system, where space starts, the Moon and stars. Items spread across Earth as a planet (p1, p3, m4), the solar system (p2, p5, m1, m6, m7, m8), space versus air (p4, m2, m5) and stars outside it (m3) with no repeated stems.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android light and 1200 px desktop dark screenshots of every step before and after Show me. At 360 px the rocket sky keeps its labels in white pills on the sky colours, the sort card sits above two half-width boxes, the zoom fills the canvas with the caption pills top and bottom, the solar system circle and Far away column fit side by side with the card above, and the moving planets fit inside the canvas with the 8 planet buttons below; nothing is clipped.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Fly higher, each card with In the air or Out in space, Zoom out, each card with in our solar system or far away, eight planet name buttons and three name choices. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action. The planet animation stops under reduced motion. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.
